# Wave005 author A: exact calculation across daily anchors

**Independent first draft, 2026-10-15.** Two concrete refinements, **zero claimed new HYPs**. I used fixed prior `331b1ae29f3e484516893204a4f990c9372f2c25`, including backlog, rounds002/009/012/033, the manual18 registry, `manual_features.py` and `feature_programs.py`. No peer005 report or current brainstorm journal was read. The 17-agent team was at capacity, so no helper was added; Root will appoint a separate skeptic. This is source research plus tiny invented arithmetic, not an implementation or experiment allowance. Current015, B41, frozen R2/W, Q/C, source and CLOSED heldouts are unchanged.

The existing compiler already groups filtered aggregates by grain/anchor, shares daily membership/metadata tables, and uses semijoins. HYP-046 already proposes an exact shared DAG; rounds012/033 already require the unchanged005 shared plan as the timing control and charge physical state/output costs. Ordinary caching, CSE, grouped aggregation and “one SQL call” are therefore rejected as new mechanisms. The narrower question is whether the compiler can exploit **the entire fixed anchor schedule** and **the operator's exact sufficient state** without changing any output.

## Primary evidence and its limits

[DBSP, VLDB Journal2025](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00778-025-00922-y), published8May2025, describes compositional automatic incrementalization. I inspected its publisher abstract/metadata; subscription full text was not available. Its [author compiler documentation/code](https://github.com/feldera/feldera/blob/main/sql-to-dbsp-compiler/using.md) exposes SQL→incremental change-stream compilation. The [author distinct operator](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/feldera/feldera/main/crates/dbsp/src/operator/distinct.rs) distinguishes a batch's positive-weight set from incremental changes to the accumulated relation. These establish mechanisms and an implementation boundary, not our cost or adoption of Feldera.

Two primary2024 engineering records sharpen the caveats. [Feldera's lifetime analysis](https://www.feldera.com/blog/time-series) requires true source properties such as append-only input and bounded disorder before discarding state. [Issue1768](https://github.com/feldera/feldera/issues/1768) records identical temporal input maps creating three separate rolling traces, closed via1805 in May2024. A shared logical stream consequently does not prove shared physical storage. I did not inspect the linked patch successfully and do not claim its current implementation details.

[DuckDB's February2025 author article](https://duckdb.org/2025/02/10/window-catchup) describes optimized window DISTINCT and cases falling back to a naive implementation. In inspected [author code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/duckdb/duckdb/main/src/function/window/window_distinct_aggregator.cpp), the fast path builds previous-occurrence/merge-sort-tree state and requires no exclusion and no argument ordering. Rewriting strict-past features with `EXCLUDE GROUP` cannot simply assume this path. Current upstream code is mutable and is not proof about the project's pinned installed engine. Both proposals below are our adaptations, not algorithms or performance attributed to these sources.

## A005-01 — compile fixed anchor/window boundaries into shared count intervals

**mechanism.** Given frozen anchors A and finite windows W, construct sorted boundaries B={source_start}∪A∪{a−w:a∈A,w∈W}. Compile each raw-count leaf to counts over disjoint `[b_j,b_{j+1})` intervals, keyed by its exact grain/action/policy signature. Every raw row contributes its multiplicity to one interval for each required grain. Build cumulative counts per key; every requested `[a−w,a)` is then the difference of two boundary prefixes. Shared inputs serve all windows and days. An event exactly at a belongs to the next interval and cannot affect a's output; lower-bound equality remains included. These boundaries are not arbitrary calendar buckets: irregular anchors create additional boundaries.

Observed recency and first-seen state have separate full-prefix min/max reducers and never expire with finite counts. Candidate metadata retains the **whole latest global timestamp bucket**, including known/NULL category mixtures from other users. Category counters use historical event category, not the latest metadata category; complete category denominators are not restricted to C. Ratios, coverage and missingness remain final typed projections. Membership can be restricted only using a predeclared label-free union of requested users/items over the fixed workload; if that union is unavailable before replay, retain all eligible keys or defer. Unknown candidate category still yields NULL conditional features; known empty keys yield0. Frozen retrieval inputs remain passthrough, not regenerated C.

**testable_prediction.** With many anchors over overlapping source prefixes, decoding/examining source rows once and sharing count intervals should reduce repeated scan/aggregation work relative to unchanged005. It may lose when union support, sorting, interval payloads or common export dominates. There is no guaranteed speedup and no expected ranking gain: exact B/W features are the output contract.

**nearest_source_free_experiment.** First use direct-list predicates and a separate interval interpreter on ≤4096 invented rows, ≤32 users/items,15 anchors and windows24/168h; include irregular anchors, lower/upper equality, raw duplicate rows, emptyC, NULL mixtures, category moves and an off-candidate denominator contributor. Compare every core/mask and full output keys, not merely a row count. Count examined rows, interval cells, transitions, metadata buckets and complete sink writes. No SQL, producer imports or model is required for this first gate. A later separately authorized native comparison must use unchanged005, optimizerON, the same fixed B41+exact R2 registry and complete common sink; faster than the direct-list oracle alone proves little.

**benefit_task1.** This makes repeated-anchor reuse an automatically derived physical plan from typed definitions. A successful result can show correct automated calculation and a scoped CPU/state improvement; it cannot show superior feature generation, human-time savings or recommendation quality.

**Finite physical cost.** Let E be raw rows to the last anchor, G the distinct grain/action keys, P boundary points, S nonempty key/interval cells, and F emitted feature values. P≤J(L+1)+1 for J anchors and L window widths. Count dispatch is ≤6E for the six existing grains; S≤6E and dense prefix storage is at most G(P−1) counters, so sparse storage is preferable. Prefix construction is O(S) after grouping/sorting cells, and reads cost two prefix lookups per count. Metadata/first-seen, distinct support, masks, joins and O(F) writing remain paid work. Group/action keys and interval cells need encoded bytes, not just counts, before a memory claim.

Count binning alone permits unordered rows; a combined chronological pipeline with recency snapshots/last-occurrence state requires authenticated nondecreasing timestamps or a paid external sort, potentially O(ElogE) comparisons and O(E) spill. That cost can erase the benefit. No late-row dropping is permitted. Reading once is not bounded memory: union keys, latest metadata buckets and high-cardinality supports can exceed8GiB. Logical scan count does not establish physical bytes/pages read, and existing005 may already prune source partitions. Retain failed/censored attempts.

**newvsrefine / knownoldIDs.** Refinement of HYP-046 and TLAB-005/016; type/identity obligations already in HYP-002 and round009, honest timing already in round012. It adds a finite-anchor interval representation and explicit cost comparison, not a canonical new hypothesis. The future compiler/measurement gate is independent of finishing015.

## A005-02 — specialize exact multiwindow DISTINCT to last occurrence

**mechanism.** For an append-only prefix already processed through all events `<a`, a value v is present in `[a−w,a)` iff its latest qualifying occurrence ℓ(v) is at least a−w. Compile DISTINCT leaves sharing grain, action, projected nominal value and NULL/filter policy into one last-occurrence map. On a new occurrence, move that value's membership from its old boundary interval to the new interval. Maintain interval counts with prefix/rank lookup; windows24/168h share this state. Repeated rows in the same interval do not add DISTINCT memberships. Raw COUNT keeps its independent multiplicity counters.

At each anchor, snapshot before ingesting **any global timestamp peer** at a. Evict a value only when its latest occurrence is strictly below the largest remaining required window's lower frontier; an older occurrence expiring must not delete a value reobserved later. An intrusive per-interval membership list with removal on a move avoids an unbounded queue of stale expiry notices. Full-prefix recency/metadata remain independent. NULL projection follows COUNT(DISTINCT)'s NULL-skipping policy, whereas NULL candidate category remains an unavailable conditional key. Sharing across different actions, projections, source policies or missingness contracts is forbidden.

**testable_prediction.** For repeated interactions, retained memberships approach the number of distinct `(grain-key,action,value)` triples within the maximum active window, rather than the number of raw occurrences or separate per-window multiplicity traces. Benefit disappears on nearly unique data; pointer/hash overhead can make it worse. It applies only to monotone anchor replay and immutable append-only events, not arbitrary deletions, corrections or time travel.

**nearest_source_free_experiment.** Compare direct sets, a generic exact multiplicity/expiry implementation, and the specialized map on the same tiny input; then fixed4096-row repeated-value and all-unique controls. Explicitly test a value duplicated across days, renewed before its old expiry, same-second duplicates, NULL, shuffled global peers and appended future suffix. Both filters must agree at every anchor/window; record live keys, live expiry entries, moves and storage bytes. Test a source retraction as an expected **unsupported-plan rejection**, not a misleading successful result. No native engine is needed. Only after correctness may a future cost pilot assess unchanged005 against A005-01 with generic distinct and with specialization, all with the same complete B/W outputs.

**benefit_task1.** The compiler chooses sufficient state from declared operator/source properties, making exact DISTINCT support explicit rather than assuming all aggregates have reversible sums. This is an operator specialization inside the same physical automation family; it supplies no additional predictive information.

**Finite physical cost.** D active distinct triples require a map entry plus one live interval-membership entry each. Prefix/rank state costs O(P) per nonempty distinct group, or sparse equivalent; do not hide that factor behind O(D). Each relevant raw row is examined once; at most two distinct projections per row are needed for the current user/item vocabulary. Membership moves cost O(logP) with an indexed count structure, unchanged intervals can avoid a move, and each retained value is evicted once before a possible later reinsertion. Window readout is O(logP) per group/window plus O(F) final broadcast/sink. Distinct-state key count may still scale with E; no cardinality-independent memory bound is claimed. Primitive schemas outside this whitelist fall back to a reviewed exact operator, not approximation.

**newvsrefine / knownoldIDs.** Refinement/suboperator of HYP-046 and existing TLAB-005 exact-distinct semantics. Last-occurrence sufficiency is not claimed as an academic invention. Its distinct value here is a typed, multiwindow physical specialization and a head-to-head state/cost falsifier. No extra HYP or native budget follows.

## Executed literal evidence and next decision

A standard-library-only probe used12 invented events,8 anchors, windows1/7 **days**,15 boundary points, and all six count grains. All16 count-dictionary comparisons and16 user/item DISTINCT-dictionary comparisons matched independent direct predicates. The input contains duplicates, expiry, same-second peers and NULL metadata. Before anchor2, item1 has3 raw views but1 distinct viewer; summing daily distinct counts gives2 and is wrong. Its latest category is10 at anchor2, then a known20/NULL global peer bucket makes it unavailable/ambiguous at anchor3. The complete category10 denominator is4 versus3 after an invalid candidate-only filter. The ledger retains the exact input and scope. This validates tiny algebraic/state witnesses, **not** the full B41/R2 compiler or throughput. Peer-permutation/future-suffix and bounded generated-shape tests remain the next gate.

Two further counterexamples delimit admission: after occurrences x@0,x@1, deleting x@1 requires recovering0, which a single last-occurrence value cannot do; and taking last occurrence over the entire future source before snapshot a leaks later state. Source-property checks and chronological snapshots are mandatory.

Prospective source-free gate: ≤4096 generated rows,15 anchors,2 windows,0 fits,≤60 process-CPU seconds and128MiB; every setup/oracle/output/failure counts. These are proposed stop caps, not authorization or feasibility measurements. Pass yields a candidate for engine design; semantic failure rejects the rewrite; equal state/work keeps correctness only; worse physical cost closes the efficiency claim. Any later timing must keep round012's balanced setup/cache/common-sink discipline and include sort, validation, metadata, preparation, serialization and cleanup. Both mechanisms remain **candidate/refinement awaiting independent skeptic**, with no prerequisite added to015 and no new ongoing experiment.

# Wave005 primary helper: SUDAF, conditional refinement

Read-only source investigation, 2026-10-15. No peer005 reports/journal, repository data, SQL, Y, models, native ML, fits, downloads, paid APIs, or shared edits. One tiny owned stdlib literal was executed.

## Primary mechanism and provenance

[Zhang and Toumani, TODS 49(2), article 7, 10 April 2024](https://doi.org/10.1145/3649133), “Sharing Queries with Nonequivalent User-defined Aggregate Functions,” exposes aggregation semantics as canonical partial states. Sharing is justified when a computable scalar function derives the requested state from a stored state for every admitted input multiset. SUDAF restricts its expression language because unrestricted sharing is undecidable. Section 6 extends state reuse to query rewrites using partial-aggregate views; different aggregate functions can share verified intermediate states. This is aggregation-expression derivation, beyond reusing an identical groupby or temporal pane. It is not an exact sliding-expiry algorithm or a universal cost-optimal operator scheduler. Its primitives include summation/product and composed scalar operations; exact distinct is not established. A practical transfer should whitelist proved derivations and charge planning/materialization costs, rather than implement arbitrary symbolic equivalence. These statements were inspected in the publisher’s primary search rendering; direct ACM open returned 403. [Primary article](https://doi.org/10.1145/3649133).

The [author homepage](https://chaozhang-cs.github.io/) lists the 2024 article alongside SUDAF ICDE 2020 and EDBT 2020 predecessors: do not label the underlying principle new in 2024. The [EDBT 2020 paper](https://openproceedings.org/2020/conf/edbt/paper_120.pdf) cites `CHAOHIT/SUDAF` for a technical-report PDF, which does not prove that executable code exists. [Repository URL](https://github.com/CHAOHIT/SUDAF), raw README and API metadata were inaccessible in this tool session. No author-code ownership, current commit, implementation equivalence, or2024 artifact release was verified. Therefore this helper fails a mandatory “accessible original paper plus author code” gate; retain as conditional conceptual evidence. A bounded search found a separate hybrid MQO paper with [author-cited repository redirect](https://github.com/vasudevrb/mqo), but its implementation was not audited and is not substituted silently.

## Exact typed adaptation: reviewer proposal, not paper guarantee

A shared node must include grouping key, predicate, raw-row multiplicity, NULL admission, exact interval/cutoff, dtype, and arithmetic semantics. For one identical non-NULL bag, `(n, sum(x), sum(x²))` derives mean and population variance. Keep raw count separately. Empty/all-NULL mean and variance return NULL under the chosen contract. Do not convert NULL to 0 or deduplicate repeated events.

All rows at a global timestamp form one peer block: answer every anchor at`t` before inserting any row timestamped`t`. Windows are `[t−W,t)`; expire rows strictly below`t−W`. Sharing a final long-window state does not reconstruct a shorter window automatically. Expiry requires retained event contributions or equivalent exact indexed boundaries. Arbitrary late arrivals require an explicit completeness/watermark contract.

Exact distinct needs keyed occurrence counts plus expiry witnesses; two panes containing the same ID cannot add their distinct counts. Bags`(0,0,3,3)` and`(0,1,1,4)` both have`n=4,sum=6,sumSquares=18`, while distinct counts are 2 and 3. Thus moments cannot derive distinct. State grows with active distinct IDs/events; no constant-memory exact-distinct claim. Rational equivalence also does not establish bitwise equality after floating-point reassociation.

## Cheapest falsifier and matched cost

[Literal JSON](/tmp/tlab-wave005-models-a-primary-helper-literal.json): six owned events, two windows, three cuts; duplicate rows, NULL, timestamp peers, and inclusive lower expiry. Actual shared and separate incremental mean/variance accumulators match a direct Fraction oracle at all six snapshots. Both arms decode the same six rows once. Executed accumulator additions/subtractions:45 shared versus75 separate; this excludes squaring, finalization, queues, decoding, memory and planning, so is not measured speedup. Strict-upper endpoint incorrectly includes two extra peers; wrong lower expiry incorrectly removes two rows. The distinct-state counterexample and empty-state NULL guard pass.

Future physical control: identical source files, projected columns, decode order, output features and cutoff/NULL/duplicate contracts in both arms; baseline already shares one scan and sorting. Charge decoding, sorting, intermediate writes/reads, build, lookups, materialization, expiry and peak resident state. Reject over-cap complete inputs; never truncate a required history. This source-only check establishes algebra and failure cases, not repository integration or useful real-data savings.

# Research lab, round 002: candidate-conditioned программы и стоимость реляционной автоматизации

15 октября 2026. Literature/generalization round, отдельный от 58 тематических записок. **Результат — проект эксперимента, не измеренное улучшение.** Прочитаны [backlog](../backlog.md), [round 001](round-001.md), его [review](round-001-review.md), feature synthesis и user–item profiles/audience. Статусы ниже предлагаются координатору; только он изменяет canonical backlog. Repo, Git, код, dependencies и raw не изменялись; модели и архивы не скачивались, обучения/API-вызовов нет.

## Четыре первичных основания

**1. Hoang Thanh Lam, Johann-Michael Thiebaut, Mathieu Sinn, Bei Chen, Tiep Mai, Oznur Alkan, 2017, One button machine for automating feature engineering in relational databases.** OneBM различает типы коллекций после join: multiset, sequence, time series; выбирает преобразования по типу, ограничивает глубину, кэширует общие префиксы и удаляет эквивалентные пути. Раздел III-A4 прямо предусматривает prediction cutoff. Однако усечение большого join до последних строк меняет вычисляемый объект; эту оптимизацию нельзя выдавать за точный оператор. Источник поддерживает typed relational generation, но не доказывает superiority при нашем CPU budget или ranking estimand. [Авторский текст, разделы III–V](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.00327v1).

**2. Joshua Robinson et al., 2024, RelBench: A Benchmark for Deep Learning on Relational Databases, NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks.** Временные predictive tasks, связи primary/foreign key и temporal neighbor sampling полезны как ориентир контракта. Рекомендационные таблицы сравнивают GNN с popularity/past-visit/LightGBM; экспертный feature-engineering user study описан отдельно. Это результаты конкретных моделей и задач, а не доказательство качества нашего search DSL. Не следует переносить ни опубликованные MAP, ни выигрыш GNN на NDCG нашего fixed-C ranking. [Первичный PDF, §§3–5](https://cs.stanford.edu/people/jure/pubs/relbench-neurips24.pdf), [официальное издание](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/25cd345233c65fac1fec0ce61d0f7836-Abstract-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.html).

**3. Ahmet Kara, Milos Nikolic, Dan Olteanu, Haozhe Zhang, F-IVM: Analytics over Relational Databases under Updates, препринт 2023, версия 2024.** Работа сочетает факторизацию, incremental view maintenance и ring payloads для joins/aggregates и статистик обучения. Из неё следует возможность разделять промежуточные вычисления, а не гарантированный speedup любого generated feature. Особенно нельзя переносить обратимость sum на rolling max/median/distinct: expiration требует собственного состояния. Наш pilot заимствует принцип, не устанавливает F-IVM/DBToaster. [Авторский PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.08583), [авторская страница проекта](https://fdbresearch.github.io/ivm.html).

**4. Yael Amsterdamer, Daniel Deutch, Val Tannen, 2011, Provenance for Aggregate Queries.** Авторы показывают, почему tuple-level аннотаций недостаточно для общей агрегации, и описывают provenance вычисленных значений. Это основание фиксировать происхождение scalar и его знаменателя; оно не является готовым temporal checker. Полные symbolic polynomials для всех реальных строк здесь не предлагаются. [Первичный PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.1110).

## Общее решение и ledger

**Предложение:** DSL хранит grain, ключи, unit, event family, set/multiset, окно, metadata policy, cutoff и свободные переменные `{u,i,t}`. При компиляции отмечать `query-constant`, `item-only` и `candidate-conditioned`. Это описания зависимости, не фильтр «бесполезных» features: query-constant может помогать boosting через interactions. Для `p_i−r_u` standalone порядок совпадает с `p_i`; HYP-011 уже честно признаёт этот предел.

Контроль B — существующий **сильно настроенный manual boosting**, с документированными bounded tuning и выбранными ручными блоками. Initial TLAB-008 с двумя fits остаётся smoke. До любых 008/009 fits: selection **22–23 октября**, confirmation **24–25** закрыта для baseline/loss/блоков/grammar/порогов. Fit cutoff, label maturity и available_at согласованы. Final test закрыт; уже раскрытая confirmation не переиспользуется следующим round.

Единственный лимит TLAB-016: **≤12 новых scalar columns, ≤4 fits, ≤2 CPU-часов**, 2 threads, RSS≤8 GiB. Здесь CPU — суммарное user+system всех дочерних процессов; wall time записывается отдельно, дополнительно stop через 120 минут. Preparation, failed runs, repair, oracle, selector и confirmation scoring оплачиваются. HYP-045 **заменяет** G/S/A либо residual ветвь round001, не складывается с ними. Если 016 уже потратил бюджет, сначала пересчитать остаток; четыре новых fits автоматически не разрешены. Новое обучение B внутри 016 тоже уменьшает этот остаток.

## HYP-045 — reference по истории, условной на кандидате

Официальное описание optimizer включает common-subexpression extraction из projection/filter. Это локальная возможность, не обещание общего кэша между отдельными SQL statements. Current005 действительно создаёт несколько statements: общий DAG может помогать между ними, но optimizer уже способен устранять часть повторений внутри statement. Нужны physical plans обоих вариантов, optimizer включён симметрично. [DuckDB internals](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/internals/overview). Lock проекта закрепляет1.5.6; current documentation описывает механизм, а конкретные APIs/plans следует проверить в этой версии перед опытом.

**Kalibera, Jones, ISMM2013:** повторения нужны на уровне, где возникает неопределённость, например отдельных запусков, а не только внутренних итераций одного процесса. [Author Accepted Manuscript, University of Kent](https://kar.kent.ac.uk/33611/45/p63-kaliber.pdf).

**OneBM** кэширует общие joining prefixes и освобождает их при обходе других ветвей; статья отдельно использует subsampling большого join, меняющий точность. В нашем exact опыте допустим первый принцип, но history truncation запрещён. **F-IVM** показывает materialized/intermediate sharing и incremental maintenance для определённых joins/aggregates; это основание исследовать reuse, не доказательство скорости snapshot compiler или rolling distinct. **Local fact:** `_grain_sql` и `create_manual_features` уже группируют features по grain/anchor, совместно вычисляют FILTER aggregates, переиспользуют metadata и distinct user/item sets через SEMI JOIN. PeakRSS измерять для каждого fresh worker, engine buffer/spill — дополнительная диагностика. Lifetime high-water одного reused процесса не позволяет честно приписать память второму плану.

Эти counters не заменяют бюджет процесса. Отдельный profiled run оплачивается; instrumentation либо одинакова у обоих, либо оба primary runs без неё. [Metrics](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/dev/metrics), [EXPLAIN ANALYZE](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/guides/meta/explain_analyze).

Cache policy объявить честно: fresh engine не означает cold OS page cache; предварительный source hashing сам может прогреть страницы. Не очищать системный cache скрыто. Фиксируются version/settings/process/thread count, порядок, concurrent workload и thermal/order drift. Если порядок меняет вывод, timing inconclusive. Если A быстрее только O, доказан выигрыш над oracle implementation. Если быстрее M, вывод ограничен pinned engine/input/schema/cache policy и measured boundary.

`create_manual_features` собирает nonratio definitions в `by_grain` и выполняет отдельный SQL batch для каждого grain/anchor. `_grain_sql` выбирает общий нижний bound: source_start, если в этом grain есть хотя бы одна observed-recency; иначе max(source_start,t−largest_window). Pair semi-join ограничивает **users из Q**, затем группирует все их past `(user,item)`; он не semi-join по C pairs. | L06: R(P,cart)+missing, N(I,cart,24h),3cols | Pair full-prefix; item168h | Cart max state, scalar NULL mask после join, item count state |
| L01: N(U,view/cart/purchase,24h),3cols | User168h | Три filtered counts на user group |

**Ни один выбранный primitive не расширяет SQL time bounds и не добавляет новый grain batch.** Это доказуемое свойство emitted statement construction, не доказательство равных physical IO/runtime. Plan selection, vector work, aggregate payload и последующая materialization могут измениться.

24h count не выводится из168h count: два одинаковых weekly totals могут иметь разное распределение по последним суткам. L05viewers24h не равен existing viewers168h; purchase-users24h не равен retrieval purchase-users168h. Поэтому semantic dedup не удаляет эти definitions. Полезность/корреляция не проверяются для оправдания pruning после metrics.

## Physical closure не равна aggregate state

[DuckDB aggregate semantics](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/sql/functions/aggregates) различают raw count и DISTINCT; max нечувствителен к дубликатам. L02/L01 counts требуют обновлений scalar counters, L06cart recency — scalar max, mask — scalar projection, а не ещё одного event aggregation. L05distinct требует различать projected users внутри каждого filtered item population; нельзя складывать daily uniques или заменить distinct rawcount ради стоимости.

[DuckDB grouped-aggregation design](https://duckdb.org/2022/03/07/aggregate-hashtable) описывает group keys и aggregate states в hash payload, thread-local aggregation/merge. Отсюда гипотеза: L05 сильнее чувствителен к числу qualifying unique `(item,user)` и skew, чем три обычных counts. Counterhypothesis: таких users мало либо scan/common context доминируют, поэтому marginal time/RSS окажутся небольшими. Фактическое sharing distinct internals конкретной версии/filters статически не установлено; «одинаковый projected column» не гарантирует один shared set.

Ровно3new physical columns каждого bundle — schema/model-width constraint, а не одинаковая память. L06 имеет2new cores+1mask; остальные —3cores. Если будущий execution действительно материализует union всех четырёх selected bundles один раз, это11new aggregate cores+1mask, а не12aggregate states и не четыре независимых base recalculations. Но сам факт union/caching должен быть подтверждён actual execution lineage; здесь он не объявляется реализованным.

[Robust External Hash Aggregation](https://duckdb.org/pdf/ICDE2024-kuiper-boncz-muehleisen-out-of-core.pdf) объясняет давление intermediates и spilling. Он не гарантирует, что наш pinned runtime завершит все aggregates в cap, не доказывает marginal speed и не разрешает увеличить memory/spill limits. Мало output columns не ограничивает group cardinality или distinct support.

## Общий overhead и конкурирующие cost hypotheses

005всегда строит latest-global-past metadata для C-products: full-prefix first/last state, rejoin всего последнего timestamp bucket, conflict/NULL resolution. Отдельный user_state получает first_seen всех Q-users. Even noncategory bundles наследуют эту работу через полный B/context; нельзя убрать её в одном плече и назвать сравнение одинаковым. Совпадающие24/168windows переиспользуют output coverage, новых coverage columns нет; это не отменяет aggregate work.

После batches005LEFT JOINs/broadcast формируют все physical Frows, добавляют masks, INSERT материализует итог; range checks идут по каждому core, затем missing summary. Wrapper экспортирует полный ordered Parquet/ZSTD и хеширует output. Три добавленные колонки увеличивают payload проверки/записи/чтения, даже при прежнем количестве строк. Гипотеза common metadata/joins/export dominance конкурирует с aggregate-state dominance; ни одна сейчас не измерена.

[DuckDB performance guidance](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/guides/performance/how_to_tune_workloads) предупреждает о blocking operators, взаимодействии memory pressure и важности cache/connection context. Тёплые pages не равны кэшированным готовым feature tables. Повторный005run заново создаёт batches; shared hash/provenance preparation учитывается один раз только если реально выполнен один раз, per-arm reads/exports — каждый раз. Нельзя ни приписать четырём arms одну бесплатную materialization без evidence, ни четырежды начислить уже однократно оплаченный common stage.

## Только prospective проверка внутри существующего cap

Если отдельная optional cost check уже помещается в016budget, сравнивать baseline-only с B+3 конкретного bundle: exact Q/C/anchors/source/registry-B, pinned version, optimizerON, threads/memory/spill policy, **полный одинаковый common sink** с необходимой дельтой колонок. Никаких одноfeature-loop baseline, LIMIT1, droppedB/context, уменьшенной C или новой серии repeats. Не хватает остатка бюджета — cost hypothesis остаётся unmeasured, без расширения квоты.

[Profiling docs](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/dev/profiling) отличают EXPLAIN от выполняющего запрос EXPLAIN ANALYZE. Будущая instrumentation, только поддержанная pinned version, должна сохранить grain statements/bounds, actual scan/operator cardinalities, aggregate/projection/join/export timings, peak buffer/temp и process CPU/RSS/wall через cleanup. Operator timings не складывать с inclusive parents и не выдавать за OS process CPU; profiler overhead тоже входит в ledger. Wrong keys/values→integrity STOP; resource failure→censored attempt, без retry/refill под видом measurement.

Основной016claim остаётся schema→typedAST generation/selection и независимая правильность расчёта. Этот разбор даёт конкретные cost hypotheses и опровергает «shared columns бесплатны», но не доказывает DAG speedup, latency gain, экономию human-hours или качество новых признаков.
